_legend: READ claude/SCAN.md FIRST, then FINDINGS.md, then this. Sections: meta | watermark=last row seen, pull only newer | deploy=live md5 and how to prove it | agent=the tools and what each verdict permits | tests=open hypotheses with readout dates | closed=settled, do not reopen | corrections=what was said and later retracted | baselines=rolling numbers | tiers=exact tier contents | asked=open client questions | hygiene=fixed data and UI faults | traps=things that will waste your time | todo=pending work
_howto: Christopher types /scan and that runs .claude/commands/scan.md. Do not do the arithmetic by hand: node claude/tools/scan.js does it and writes claude/SCAN.md. python is NOT on PATH in git-bash here, node is.

closed.evidence: The counter is a RUNNING DAILY TOTAL, so the day's dose is the last non-zero row of that day. Every day from Aug 1 to Aug 19 reads 1300mg or less. traps: TIME: timeLocal is her wall clock. The ISO timestamp is 2 hours ahead of America/Vancouver because her device sits at UTC-5. stamp() builds both from the device. Her own typed times (Jul 22 'about 10:00 pm' on a 10:41 PM row, Jul 24 '8;00 pm' on an 8:01 PM row, Jul 26 '12:00' on a 12:24 PM row, Jul 27 '9:00 pm' on a 9:13 PM row) prove timeLocal is the real one. Use timeLocal for everything. Never convert the ISO field.
FOOD: a food row's time is when she pressed save, NOT when she ate. The meal log has an eat-time field that lands in the row as '· ate 7:30'. When it is there it wins.
COUNTERS: Tylenol, magnesium and gummy tiles are running daily totals. Last non-zero row of the local day IS the day's dose. Never add sessions.

MAGNESIUM: her dose is 200mg every SECOND night. Check the RUN, not the night. Four nights in a row is a different exposure from one night. Cross every supplement against gut days at lag 0, lag 1 and lag 2, and as a run length.

NEVER let the app stop her recording what actually happened. The Tylenol boxes did it, the sauerkraut tile did it, and the magnesium skip night nearly did it. An interface that argues with the patient produces a record that lies. Tell her the rule, then let her log the truth.

A BLANK IS NOT A ZERO. A day she did not tick her supplements is unknown, not empty. Comparing against those days makes every daily supplement look like a cause, because the comparison group is really days she did not open the app. The day table enforces this per variable. Never do this analysis by eye.

ONE INSTRUCTION, ONE SOURCE. An instruction written in two places will eventually contradict itself, and she follows the TILE, not the card, because the tile is where she taps. Drive both from one switch or do not write it twice.
Her night reading needs NOTHING from us. Her gaps are 3.0, 3.2 and 2.9 hours. She always tests past two hours, exactly as she said on Aug 21. Never ask her for a fixed gap again.

EVERY PAUSE NEEDS AN END POINT ON THE SCREEN. Sauerkraut had a date and she followed it. Magnesium did not and she had to ask. If you take something away from her, the tile must say what brings it back.

EDIT SCRIPTS MUST WRITE BEFORE THEY CAN FAIL, or verify after. On Aug 22 an edit script applied change A, then hit a no-match on change B and process.exit(1) before fs.writeFileSync. Change A was silently lost and the tile shipped with the old text while the card shipped with the new one. The md5 changed, the deploy verified, and the screens still disagreed. ALWAYS re-read the live page for the actual STRINGS, never just the md5.
A SUPPLEMENT ASK FROM HER IS A PROTOCOL CHANGE REQUEST, not a comment. Action it or answer it the same day. Her K2 correction sat unread for five days.

DO NOT NAG is a limit on MY guessing, not a veto on her asking. On Aug 26 she asked in capitals to be kept on about her salt, one day after I told her I would stop. She is the patient and she knows what helps her.

CHECK WHAT A CONTROL ACTUALLY MEASURES BEFORE BUILDING ON IT. Three times this month a control meant something other than its label: the Tylenol counter, the one-tap meal button, and the Water and salt tile.

dataLayer.build: node claude/tools/build-day-table.js   (add --cache to reuse the last pull)
dataLayer.readFirst: claude/fh-signals.md. It is arithmetic, not conclusion. Read it BEFORE FINDINGS.md and before touching raw rows.
rules: A blank is not a zero. Days she did not record the cause or the outcome are dropped, per variable.
Every exposure tested at lag 0, 1 and 2, and as a run length.
Nothing reported under 5 exposed days and 5 clean days.
All outputs live in claude/, which is gitignored. The repo is public and these are her medical record.
dataLayer.tokenNote: The scan reads a 3 KB signals file instead of 180 KB of raw rows. The arithmetic is in the script, where it cannot be misremembered.
dataLayer.timezone: Self-calibrating. calibrate() reads the offset back out of her own rows by comparing each ISO instant to the wall clock her device wrote. Current reading: UTC-5, 962 votes to 1. Never hardcode it again.
dataLayer.confoundGuard: If an exposure's days sit in one contiguous recent block, the row is marked TIME CONFOUND. Sauerkraut vs fasting scored 10x and is confounded: sauerkraut started Aug 11 and the fasting drift started Aug 11. Treat marked rows as questions.

agent.why: Six wrong calls in five days, all the same shape: a conclusion written before the arithmetic that would test it. None was a gap in knowledge. Prose rules can be reasoned past. Code rules cannot.
agent.readFirst: claude/SCAN.md. Generated, cannot go stale. Read it BEFORE FINDINGS.md. Where they disagree, SCAN.md wins.
agent.run: node claude/tools/scan.js   (add --cache to reuse the last pull)

pieces.claude/tools/guards.js: 7 guards, each named with the date it was earned and what it cost. The scan STOPS if one trips. Caught a real parser bug on its first run: a typed eat time of Noon was being thrown away, the third instance of reading a button press instead of her own words.
pieces.claude/tools/claim.js: The claim gate. No causal statement reaches her screen except through it. Checks: enough event days, enough exposed and clean days, lift, a required mechanism, Fisher exact p, a multiple-comparison correction, a time-confound check, and a WASHOUT check that lets a removal beat a correlation.
pieces.claude/tools/scan.js: The scan as a program. 861 cause and outcome pairs at three lags, all through the gate, into claude/SCAN.md.
pieces.claude/tools/verify-live.js: Proves the live page says the exact words intended. A checksum proves something shipped, not the right thing.
pieces.claude/tools/test-gate.js: Re-runs this week four wrong claims through the gate. All four are stopped. The one right claim ships. Run it after any change to claim.js.
